prompt: Roadmap III, Prompt 218, Part A: binary masses and radii, the SB2-plus-eclipse chain (tranche T3 by D-R10-207-01)
committed: before js/inference/binaryMasses.js, the inference models, the validator, the pinned oracle results, the ensembles, any panel or any lesson of Prompt 218 existed. The systems, seeds, cadences and noise below are written out so that the oracle (numpy, scipy, batman: no Gravitas code) builds its own data and the harness builds the same systems; nothing was tuned against the kernel, which did not exist.
rule: A crossed bound is a failed check, recorded in failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured is NOT RUN and says why.

constants.note: IAU 2012 B2 (au), IAU 2015 B3 (nominal solar GM and radius). Masses are computed as 4 pi^2 a^3 / (GM_sun P^2), so no value of G enters a mass. log g uses GM_sun / R^2.

scope.built: double-lined spectroscopic orbits (two radial-velocity curves of one orbit with a shared period, phase, e cos w and e sin w, each star's semi-amplitude, one systemic velocity and an optional offset between the stars) through js/inference/rv.js's curve; the mass ratio, the minimum masses M sin^3 i and a sin i (labelled minimum); the single-lined mass function and a companion's minimum mass for a stated primary mass; and the joint eclipsing-plus-spectroscopic solution, one fit with the eclipse light curve and both radial-velocity curves sharing the orbit (absolute masses, radii, a, log g with the covariance of the whole fit carried through).
scope.notBuilt: the visual-binary branch (Part B, gated), an absolute mass from a single-lined system, a temperature or luminosity as a fitted quantity (they are inputs, labelled), gravitational redshift, light-travel time, tidal distortion, spots, third bodies, rotational broadening; the fitted velocities are taken as given, not measured from spectra.

convention: Star 1 is the star eclipsed at the primary eclipse, star 2 in front of it at the time tc of that conjunction (the convention of Prompt 217: BINARIES.md). w is the argument of periastron of the orbit of star 2 relative to star 1, the primary eclipse at true anomaly pi/2 - w (Winn 2010). The line-of-sight velocity is positive for receding. Star 1's velocity is gamma + K1 [cos(f + w) + e cos w] and star 2's is gamma - K2 [cos(f + w) + e cos w]: star 1 recedes before the primary eclipse and approaches after it. K1 and K2 are positive, K1/K2 = M2/M1.

X1.what: circular, total/annular primary, star 2 smaller (F stars)

G1.what: X1's stars at an inclination where the minimum sky separation is about 0.93 of R1 + R2: a thin lens, the radii a valley of rsum, k and inc

sampling.flux: regular, one point every 30 minutes (1/48 d), from tc - 0.15 P to tc - 0.15 P + 4 P, no exposure smearing
sampling.rv: 20 epochs per star, drawn uniformly over the same span by the seeded stream, both stars measured at every epoch

sb2Only.use: C1 (the radial velocities alone, no light curve)

checks.what: the closed case, two stars of 1 solar mass on a circular orbit of radius 1 au (P from Kepler's third law with the nominal GM, inc 90, K1 = K2 = pi a / P with a the separation): the chain returns each mass 1.0, a 1 au in solar radii and the mass ratio 1; and the forward map from (M1, M2, R1, R2, P, e, w, inc) to (K1, K2, rsum, k, ...) composed with the chain returns M1, M2, R1, R2 and a for X1, X2, X3

the minimum masses M sin^3 i computed from the amplitudes equal the true masses times sin^3 i at inc 60, 75 and 89.2 degrees (a sin i likewise), and the absolute mass is the minimum mass divided by sin^3 i: nothing is returned as a mass without an inclination

the single-lined mass function f = P K1^3 (1 - e^2)^(3/2) / (2 pi G) in the nominal-GM form equals M2^3 sin^3 i / (M1 + M2)^2 for X1, X2, X3; the companion's minimum mass for the true M1 solves M2^3 = f (M1 + M2)^2, is at most the true M2 and satisfies that equation

the eccentric radial-velocity curve of star 1 has its extrema at gamma + K1 (1 + e cos w) and gamma + K1 (-1 + e cos w) (sampled on 20000 phases), and at every time (v1 - gamma) / (v2 - gamma) = -K1 / K2 (the barycentre does not move)

at the primary conjunction the circular curves cross gamma: |v1 - gamma| and |v2 - gamma| below 1e-9 km/s; star 1 is receding (above gamma) a hundredth of a period before it and approaching after, star 2 the opposite
the Sun by the nominal values: log10 g (cgs) = 4.438 within 0.001, and a star of 1 solar mass and 2 solar radii has a gravity four times lower (0.60206 dex lower) within 1e-12

the radial velocities of both stars of X1, X2, X3 against a direct numerical integration of the two-body problem in three dimensions (scipy DOP853, relative tolerance 1e-12, the orbit set up from the position and velocity at periapsis, rotated by w and inc, the primary conjunction found as the root of the relative position's sky-plane X component with Z > 0, the stars' velocities from the centre-of-mass split) at 400 phases

the pinned joint solution of the oracle (scipy least_squares on its own forward models: batman for the two eclipses as in Prompt 217, the integrated two-body radial velocities, the oracle's own noise realization written to oracle-results.json) for X1 and X2: the fit of Gravitas to the same data returns M1, M2, R1, R2, a, K1, K2 and inc within 0.25 of the oracle's standard deviation of each, and a standard deviation of each within 15 percent of the oracle's
the oracle's own solution recovers the truth of its data within 3 of its standard deviations for M1, M2, R1, R2 (a check on the oracle, not on Gravitas)

radial velocities alone (the model sb2-orbit), 120 seeds of X2: the 1-sigma interval holds the truth at the stated rate for K1, K2, e cos w, e sin w, P, and for the derived mass ratio q = M2/M1, a sin i, M1 sin^3 i and M2 sin^3 i

the joint model, 100 seeds of X1: the 1-sigma interval of the fit (the covariance of the whole fit, scaled by sqrt(chi2/dof) when above 1) holds the truth at the stated rate for M1, M2, R1, R2, a, inc, K1, K2
the same on 60 seeds of X2 with e cos w and e sin w free
the median fitted M1, M2, R1, R2 over the circular joint ensemble is within 3 median sigma / sqrt(n) of the truth (no bias beyond the statistical)

only star 1's radial velocities (and the eclipse light curve) of X1: on 20 seeds the result lists no absolute mass, radius in kilometres or solar units, or mass of either star: every derived mass-like quantity is the mass function or a companion's minimum mass and its label says 'minimum' or 'mass function'

double-lined radial velocities of a non-eclipsing orbit (X1 with inc 60, flat light curve plus noise) in the model sb2-orbit: on 20 seeds every mass it returns is an M sin^3 i labelled minimum and the joint model, given the flat light curve, is refused with a message that names the missing eclipse, never fitted

the eccentric system X2's radial velocities fitted with e fixed at 0 fail the stated residual test (reduced chi-square above 1.5) on at least 95 percent of 20 seeds, and the correct model on at most 5 percent of the first 60 eccentric-ensemble seeds

the grazing system G1 (30 seeds) is flagged 'not constrained' for the radius ratio k (the rule of Prompt 217's D1, unchanged) and the result then flags the radii R1, R2 as not constrained; at least 90 percent of seeds; the control (the first 40 seeds of X1) is flagged at most 5 percent

X1 with the two stars' velocity columns exchanged (the primary's velocities labelled as star 2's): the joint fit fails the residual test (reduced chi-square above 1.5) or leaves a semi-amplitude on its bound on at least 95 percent of 20 seeds; the eclipse, not the labels, says which star is which

V505 Persei, a detached double-lined eclipsing binary (two F5 V stars), against Southworth (2021), The Observatory 141, 122 (arXiv:2106.04323), numbers only, read from the paper's HTML rendering on 2026-10-29. The contract: the light-curve geometry (rsum, k, inc, P) from the fit of the TESS Sector 18 SPOC 2-minute file under the fixed contract of Prompt 217's E1 (windows of +-1.0 T14, local straight-line normalisation, circular orbit, limb darkening 0.261 and 0.23, third light 0, fitted tc, P, rsum, k, inc, J); the published semi-amplitudes K_A = 89.12 and K_B = 90.31 km/s (Table IV, final values) with their quoted +-0.09 and +-0.12 km/s taken as their uncertainties, e = 0; the chain of this prompt; compared with the paper's Table V masses 1.2745 +- 0.0036 and 1.2577 +- 0.0030 solar masses and radii 1.2941 +- 0.0016 and 1.2637 +- 0.0017 solar radii (semi-major axis 14.984 +- 0.013). Nothing here was tuned to those values.

limits.note: Both stars' K values are the paper's measurements; the radial-velocity data themselves (Marschall 1997; Tomasella et al. 2008) are not in the repository and were not fetched, so this tests the geometry-to-masses-and-radii half of the chain on a real star and not the velocity fit. The light-curve file is not in the repository; the leg is NOT RUN without it.

checks.what: one joint fit of X1's first seed (about 700 flux rows and 40 velocities) with its profiles skipped runs in at most 20 s of CPU on the machine, recorded and not a physics bound
